document: Global Appellation and Terroir Types Definition

AOC Grand Cru.description: The absolute pinnacle of the French quality pyramid. A unique terroir classified as a fully independent and autonomous appellation.

AOC Regional.description: The foundational regional tier of a French wine region (e.g., AOC Alsace, AOC Bourgogne).

AOC Regional DGC.description: An official municipal or communal subdivision within a regional AOC, subject to stricter production and yield criteria (e.g., Alsace - Blienschwiller).

AOC Regional Lieu-dit.description: A historically recognized plot or single vineyard characterized by specific geological attributes, authorized to appear on the label under specific conditions (e.g., La Tâche).

AOC Sparkling.description: Sparkling wines produced using the traditional method, featuring a secondary fermentation inside the bottle (e.g., Champagne, Crémant).

IGP Regional.description: Territorial wines focused on geographic origin, offering higher flexibility in grape varieties and winemaking styles than the AOC tier.

IGP Regional Sub-zone.full_name: Indication Géographique Protégée - Mention de sous-zone
IGP Regional Sub-zone.description: A specific delimited sub-descriptor or community zone embedded within a broader departmental or regional IGP footprint.

AOP.description: Protected Designation of Origin for quality wines produced in specified regions of Wallonia.

IGP.description: Protected Geographical Indication for regional wines originating from Wallonia.

BOB.description: Protected Designation of Origin in Dutch, applied to quality wine appellations in Flanders.

BGA.description: Protected Geographical Indication in Dutch, applied to regional wine designations in Flanders.

DOCG.full_name: Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita
DOCG.description: The highest tier of Italian wine classification, subject to rigorous sensory analysis and protected by a numbered state seal.

DOCG UGA.description: Official municipal or specific sub-zone boundaries within a major DOCG appellation (e.g., specific communes within Chianti Classico or Barolo).

IGT.description: Country or territorial wines, equivalent to the French IGP framework, offering higher creative flexibility to winemakers.

AVA.description: An officially delimited wine-growing region in the United States defined by specific geographic, soil, and climatic features managed by the TTB.
